chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The slave's divorce is not valid, nor his marriage, except with the permission of his master. I said: 'But the master married him with his own hand, so whose is the divorce?' He said: 'With the hand of the master.' Allah has made an example of a slave who has no power over anything; the divorce is not in his hand.
ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to divorce a male slave if the master arranged his marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of 'abd' (male slave) by establishing that both marriage (nikah) and divorce (talaq) require the master's permission, emphasizing the master's retained authority even if he arranged the union. The Imam supports this ruling by citing Quran 39:29, drawing a parallel between the slave's lack of independent agency and the Quranic description of a 'servant owned by another,' thereby grounding the legal principle in scriptural exegesis.
